summary.scope: Boundary discovery, no source identities or recovered C++ claims

notes:
The 20 largest served orphan ranges yielded 22 entries. RVA 1BF200 is a continuation of the function at 1BF090, whose address is installed by the callback store at 1C19FF. The nearby 1BE770 function is distinct; both cross alignment gaps and are represented with their actual discontiguous ranges. Neither adjacency nor instruction shape was used as entry proof.

The served range at 909B7 contains three independently referenced functions, beginning at 909B7, 90F72 and 90F7D. Pointer-table references identify the split.

Two computed jumps were checked explicitly. At 6D7DD4, a 13-entry table at 6D848C matches the guard and Ghidra target set. At 6EAD27, the guard admits 107 values; the byte selector array at 6EB310 maps them into the 27 pointer slots at 6EB2A4. All selected destinations agree with the resolved flow edges. Tables and skipped alignment instructions are excluded from body bytes.

Callback stores supplied entry evidence for the SIMD routines. Register-loaded addresses were traced to their subsequent table stores with no intervening write to that register. The immediate stores at 1C4676 and 1C46A9 occur in loops over callback arrays initialized from VA E22E60 and E22D40. Original donor names or class identities remain unclaimed.

The survey covered 30 large orphan ranges; 39 reviewed entries passed. Several served ranges contained multiple independently referenced functions. Two SIMD ranges are continuations of earlier entries: 1C1E00 belongs to 1C1AD0, and 1BDAC0 belongs to 1BD980. Their callback stores provide entry evidence; skipped alignment instructions remain excluded.

Three direct switch tables were checked: 8 slots at 6EAB08, 13 slots at 6F24A8, and 16 slots at 710C24. Guard-derived index bounds and every raw table target agree with the probe's resolved flows.

Two terminal indirect dispatches required additional reasoning. Functions at 8DAE4 and 54684E restore their saved stack/registers and jump through a table loaded from a receiver. `prove_virtual_tails.py` checks every path to these endpoints and the RET cleanup of their direct callees, including the tail of 28AFA9 to 39D7CF. These establish wrapper endpoints without enumerating runtime destinations; those destinations remain unresolved. `virtual-tail-evidence.json` preserves the distinction. No body bytes are assigned to speculative callees.

Code references to 6FEFF0 and 6EDBD0 pass their addresses to 6D6500. The constructor copies the incoming argument into object offset 0x20. The reference to 14DFE5 follows an explicit MOV/JMP/PUSH/PUSH/store path, rather than an assumed linear fallthrough. Address literals in table or stack stores establish references only; no original identities are claimed.

Entry 317F0, whose body appears to include the served range at 3181E, remains outside this batch. The only exact VA-looking byte sequence at 1F7994 lies inside a CALL displacement and was rejected. A raw relative jump at 6C1BCD does target 317F0, but its enclosing unassigned region [6C1B60,6C1BD2) has not yet received independent entry evidence. The potential caller chain is saved for a separate investigation rather than counted as established.

Raw-pointer filtering is recorded in `rejected-pointer-hits.json`. Requiring nearby known entries was a triage heuristic, not a correctness rule: the tables supporting F6499 and FC04C were reviewed manually because several neighbors were themselves unmapped. The accepted address values, prologues, complete bodies and surrounding code-pointer structure support those entries.

notes:
The survey covered 40 orphan ranges; 50 entries were probed and 49 accepted. Some ranges were multiple functions; 1B8760 is a continuation of the directly registered routine at 1B8560. Entry 317F0 remains pending as described in batch 6.

Three switch dispatches were independently checked. At 35E3AD the index is EDI, guarded by CMP EDI,17 and an unsigned JA after a signed JG; the intervening branch does not modify flags. At 7105C1 a 15-slot table dispatches on EAX. At 7105DB a second 4-slot table dispatches on ESI; MOV EDI,EAX between the comparison and JA preserves flags. Every raw target matches the inferred flow edges.

Function 5463C9 is held and excluded from accepted ranges. Its two apparent virtual tail exits follow a body containing two other indirect calls. Their cleanup has not been independently established, so this pass does not assume the all-path stack restoration proved for simpler wrappers in batch 6.

The isolated data value at 8F26A8 matching VA 733031 is embedded in text and was rejected as pointer-table evidence. The actual entry 333031 is instead backed by a code argument at 335DBB passed through 747640 to 74E520, which stores the argument in a callable record. Entry 334E51 has the same reviewed registration path. Paired string/function records support 74ACE0 and 74AE00; these were reviewed separately from the contiguous code-pointer-table heuristic.

The dispatch registry is established by byte-index load at 0x7003c3, tag comparison at 0x700424, and indirect call at 0x700455. Only matching tags with executable targets are accepted; the 256-value index envelope is not claimed as the table extent.

For 0x7044c0, the bounded switch is resolved from retail bytes and supplied as transient jump references before Ghidra body inference. Capstone independently checks its guard, selector map and target set. These references are analyst supplied, not independently discovered by Ghidra.

For 0x184ad0, existing orphan instructions at 0x184f4e and 0x184f53 conflict with sequential MOVSS instructions at 0x184f49 and 0x184f51. The old instructions have no incoming saved direct-flow references or function ownership. Only that nine-byte conflicting decode is cleared transiently; the body is then inferred without a forced extent.

All entry seeds are direct-call targets from previously validated local bodies. The switch at 0x6dd56a is resolved from its CMP EAX,41 / JA guard and byte selector map. Retail table targets are supplied as transient flow references, then checked independently by Capstone. No function sizes are forced.
Entry seeds are direct-call targets from accepted bodies in the preceding batch. Targets already mapped or inside a prior body are excluded. No source identity is assigned.

Two bounded selector switches were checked against their guards and all exported Ghidra targets. Six simple wrappers have separately recorded restored-stack proofs in prove_virtual_tails.py and virtual-tail-evidence.json; their runtime virtual targets remain unresolved. Complex wrappers 0x5438d6 and 0x5463c9 are excluded because stack cleanup across their indirect calls has not been established.

notes:
Image-wide survey of aligned data-section pointers with at least two already established entries in their seven-word context. Candidates inside existing instruction bytes and earlier held candidates were excluded. Every accepted body independently passes retail decode, reachability and ownership checks.

97 wrappers have independently checked absence of calls and stack writes, ending in fixed-slot indirect dispatch. Two more wrappers use the previously checked zero-pop 0x3f81b0 helper. Their runtime targets remain unresolved; no class or source identity is assigned. Two bounded switches have checked guards and exact table targets.

Verified tail targets are expanded to a fixed point: a body can terminate at another entry only after that destination has passed the full checks. The validator asserts no previously accepted destination loses validation.

The 42-byte body at 0x36044a agrees exactly with its existing ledger range; it adds inventory coverage, not source recovery. All remaining exceptions stay excluded.

notes:
The fourth argument of destructor iterator 0x629110 is directly called at 0x62913b. The fifth argument of constructor iterator 0x629512 is forwarded by the exact push sequence at 0x629562..0x62956e to ArrayUnwind, whose fourth argument is called at 0x6290d0. Every literal callback argument is traced through its contiguous stack setup to the helper call. Entries stay anonymous; callback role is recorded separately from class or function identity.

Six literal destructor callbacks are direct five-byte trampolines. Their direct JMP targets are separately seeded and fully checked before the wrappers may terminate there. The six target bodies pass without additional exceptions.

Tables are actual literal arguments at calls to retail INI::initFromINI (0x2de78, argument 2) or MultiIniFieldParse::add (0x2bc6e, argument 1). Complete contiguous argument setup is checked before parsing records. The target lookup at 0x2bc27 advances 16 bytes at 0x2bc3d and returns the callback at record+4 at 0x2bc65; its caller invokes that result at 0x2d885. Tables must terminate, contain valid field-label strings and have executable or null callback slots. Eleven malformed/incompatible table candidates are separately recorded and excluded. Field labels remain data labels, never invented callback names.

These two entries are callback slots in the valid prefix of a table actually passed to parser helper 0x2de78. The target lookup advances through those named records and invokes each matching callback. The table continues into incompatible data without a visible sentinel: the exact extent issue is preserved in parser-table-evidence.json and each entry record. Only the valid callback records are used; no terminator or complete table extent is claimed. Field-label strings are recorded as data labels, not recovered callback names.

Literal second arguments to helper 0x2deb5 are callback entries: the target invokes that argument at 0x2ded3. Every recorded call site has a checked contiguous two-push argument path. No identity is inferred from the builder role.

RTTI table support is checked through decorated type-descriptor bytes, zero-signature complete-object locators, zero-signature class hierarchies, bounded base-class arrays and their descriptor references. Candidate slots lie in a contiguous executable-pointer run directly following the checked locator pointer. Type bytes are preserved as context only; no source body or original callback identity is assigned.

Entry references come from checked MOV [object-register], immediate-data-pointer instructions in mapped code. Only the first executable pointer at each installed address is used, so no table extent or class owner is inferred. Two indirect tails have explicit unchanged-stack proofs; one loads its callback into EDX, leaves that register intact and ends in JMP EDX. One complex indirect-call wrapper and one body overlapping an earlier map remain excluded.

notes: The wrapper entry has prior code-table evidence and transfers control through a direct five-byte JMP without changing ESP. Its explicit destination is separately seeded and validated before the wrapper is accepted as ending at that target.

Each entry is explicitly stored as a literal code address into an absolute global slot, and mapped code independently CALLs or JMPs through that exact slot. All stores and uses are checked against retail bytes. Other address stores without a traced dispatch use remain outside this batch. No class or callback name is asserted.

The literal callback is argument 3 at the checked direct call to 0x6ba7b0.
